final_candidates.decision_summary: Introduces an N-linked glycosylation motif at the Sa antigenic site that sterically blocks neutralizing antibodies while preserving HA folding and receptor-binding competence.
Reverses charge in the prominent Sa loop, abolishing critical electrostatic interactions for multiple monoclonal antibodies with minimal impact on viral replication.
Located at an exposed apical loop near the Sb/Sa boundary, charge inversion mediates potent immune escape while maintaining stable trimeric HA structure.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool converged on highly confident, well-characterized antigenic escape mutations that maintain replication fitness.

history.rationale: K169 is located in the prominent Sa antigenic site loop where charge reversal strongly disrupts neutralizing antibody binding. In deep mutational scanning of WSN HA, K169E is well-tolerated and maintains high viral replication fitness.
K169E confers potent escape from Sa-directed neutralizing antibodies via charge reversal while maintaining high fitness in WSN HA.

K176 resides within the Sa epitope on the globular head and is a known target for monoclonal antibody escape. The charge-reversal substitution confers robust immune evasion while preserving trimer stability and entry function.
K176E sits at an exposed apical loop in the Sb/Sa interface, providing broad monoclonal escape with minimal disruption to receptor binding.

S158 is an exposed residue at the crown of the Sa site loop frequently mutated in antigenic drift. S158N alters local surface epitope topology to evade humoral recognition while retaining high viral fitness.
S158N creates an N-linked glycosylation sequon (N-S-F at 158-160) that shields the Sa epitope while preserving viral replication and trimer assembly.

K170 is in the Sa antigenic loop adjacent to 169, and charge-neutralizing mutations abrogate key antibody electrostatic contacts. This substitution is well-tolerated structurally in WSN HA without impairing receptor binding.
K170N neutralizes the positive charge at the Sa boundary, commonly tolerated in natural and lab-selected drift variants.

S209 is part of the Sb antigenic site in the 190-loop flanking the receptor-binding domain. Introduction of asparagine alters antigenic presentation and facilitates immune escape while maintaining replication competency.
S209N provides antigenic variation in the Ca2 region while maintaining native-like folding stability.

K157 contributes positive electrostatic charge to the Sa epitope recognized by potent neutralizing antibodies. Charge reversal to Glu drives antibody escape while being well accommodated in HA head folding.
K157E alters Sa site electrostatics; well tolerated though slightly less frequent than K169E.
S173 is a surface-exposed residue in the Sa loop accessible to antibody paratopes. Substitution with Asn alters steric properties for immune escape with minimal impact on viral replication.
S173N modifies loop flexibility and solvent accessibility near the Sa region with benign fitness effects.
K187 lies in the Ca1 antigenic region and interacts with head-directed antibodies. Mutation to Glu reduces antibody affinity via charge repulsion while maintaining viral fitness.
K187E targets the 190-helix vicinity adjacent to Sb, but proximity to the sialic acid pocket requires caution.
R237 is a key surface-exposed basic residue within the Ca2 antigenic site. Charge reversal mediates antibody evasion while preserving necessary native conformational contacts.
R237E contributes to Ca1 site remodeling, though severe charge shifts in this turn can marginally lower replication titer.

K235 is situated in the Ca2 epitope, where loss of positive charge reduces recognition by neutralizing sera. The polar Asn substitution is well tolerated without destabilizing the hemagglutinin monomer.
K235N eliminates a basic side chain in Ca1, offering moderate escape with well-preserved assembly.
